subject: Medford Poet Laureate Vijaya Sundaram Interview
overview: Danielle Balocca interviewed Medford's second Poet Laureate, Vijaya Sundaram, regarding her creative process and community initiatives. Sundaram discussed her work writing for civic occasions, her library poetry club, and the role of the artist as a mirror for society.

items.title: Introduction and Local Favorites
items.summary: Vijaya Sundaram introduced herself as the city's second Poet Laureate and recommended Chili Garden and a new Haitian bakery on Salem Street as local dining favorites.

items.title: Role of the Poet Laureate
items.summary: Sundaram described her role as a voice for the community, which involves conducting research to write original poetry for civic events including Juneteenth and the mayoral inauguration. She suggested that the position's term should be extended from two to three years to allow for greater impact.

items.title: Community Projects and Poetry Club
items.summary: Sundaram outlined plans for local poetry open mics and detailed her Friday poetry club for teens and adults at the Medford Public Library. She also advocated for traditional leaflet campaigns to improve resident engagement with city arts events.

items.title: Artistic Identity and Allyship
items.summary: Sundaram discussed using empathy and her perspective as an Indian American poet to represent diverse experiences while acting as an ally to marginalized groups. She reflected on her career as an English professor and her belief that poetry can serve as an accessible entryway to intelligence and self-expression.

items.title: Poetry Readings
items.summary: Sundaram read several original poems, including 'Passing,' 'My Body,' a commemorative piece for Haitian Flag Day, and 'A Ruby Song.'

items.title: Local Activism and Global Perspectives
items.summary: The discussion concluded with a focus on local climate activism and Sundaram's concerns regarding the rise of nationalism and religious factionalism globally.
